clue.text: Decided what hairdresser might have done

definitions.meaning: a matter that is decided is settled beyond argument
a stylist trims and then blow-dries hair, read literally

explanation.surface: A salon customer's verdict on the stylist, offered as if it were a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something settled and certain, beyond further discussion, like a decided question.

clue.text: First form going on about great work

indicators.note: signals one piece added after the other, the second tacked onto the end

parts.note: the first year group at school is class one, written CLASS I
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A first-year school class tackling a masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is an acknowledged masterpiece, a work of lasting excellence.

clue.text: Egyptian king familiarly seen with gold coach

parts.note: Tutankhamun is popularly shortened to Tut
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: King Tut glimpsed beside a golden carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to give them private teaching, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Mobile insured to include mother and nanny

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters take another piece into their middle
letters that are mobile move about, so the word insured is rearranged

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mobile phone policy extended to cover a mother and a nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like a phone but signals the rearrangement, giving NURSEID; 'to include' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a woman employed to look after children, the same job as this older word.

clue.text: Trade board

definitions.meaning: to trade is to do business, buy and sell
a plank of pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Two terse words that could be a business heading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means doing business as a verb and also a fir or pine plank as a noun.

clue.text: Like an actor showing unfairness?

definitions.meaning: Equity is the actors' trade union

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a performer is displaying injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN EQUITY, the answer describes an actor belonging to Equity, the British performers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means injustice, a lack of fairness, its direct synonym.

clue.text: Protest over new diabolical spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the next

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest against some fresh evil force.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit or devil, which is what a diabolical spirit is.

clue.text: Navy tie modelled to present innocence

indicators.note: letters modelled are shaped anew, so navy tie is rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval tie shown off by a model to suggest innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of experience or guile, a synonym for innocence.

clue.text: Renewed fame isn't obvious

indicators.note: letters renewed are made over afresh, so fame isn't is rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment that a revived celebrity is not clearly evident.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means plain to see, clearly apparent, a synonym.

clue.text: Every second, a flier's coming in behind schedule

indicators.note: says one piece enters the other

parts.note: late means behind schedule
a tern is a sea bird, a flier; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Every second a plane is landing late at a busy airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The flier is a bird, not a plane; 'coming in' signals the insertion and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate days are every other day, so the word means every second one.

clue.text: This person's returned twice to tour a city

indicators.note: the doubled piece travels round, enclosing what follows
the reversed piece appears two times over
says the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the speaker saying 'this person is' gives I'M

explanation.surface: A traveller who has come back twice to tour a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses, 'twice' doubles the result to MIMI, and 'to tour' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city in Florida, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Test monitor

definitions.meaning: to check people for a disease or suitability

explanation.surface: Two words that might head a technician's checklist.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means examining applicants or patients as a verb and a display panel as a noun.

clue.text: Go with swimmer to find toll road

parts.note: a turn is a go in a game
the pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Taking a fish along to find a road where you pay to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a turnpike is a highway charging tolls, historically a road with a toll gate.

clue.text: Search agent, overlooking info for battle

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: overlooking something means leaving it out, so a piece is removed

parts.note: taken as written before removal
GEN is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A search agent ignoring intelligence before going into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' removes GEN from AGENT, leaving AT. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between forces, a synonym for battle.

clue.text: Abuse film superstar going topless

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, such as a mist

indicators.note: losing the top, in a down clue the first letter, is dropped

parts.note: a great is a star performer, a superstar

explanation.surface: A film star going topless on set amounts to abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the G of GREAT, leaving REAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat is to treat badly, a synonym of abuse as a verb.

clue.text: Mean to get price for trendy plan

indicators.note: says the first word receives a new piece in place of another
names what is swapped out: one piece standing for another

parts.note: a mean person is stingy
IN means fashionable
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: A miser hoping a price will fund a fashionable plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action designed to achieve a goal.

clue.text: Native sailor beginning to head east

indicators.note: the earlier piece goes on top of the next in this down clue

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
an origin is a beginning
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A local sailor setting out to sail east.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, a native.

clue.text: Disturb international organisation supported by Yorkshire Dales town

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece rests on the second

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
Settle is a market town in the Yorkshire Dales in northern England

explanation.surface: A global body backed by a small northern English town causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to make uneasy, a synonym of disturb.

clue.text: Occupant let team inside

indicators.note: one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A tenant who let a sports team into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' is the landlord's sense, to rent out; 'inside' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in a place, its occupant.

clue.text: Burden umpire with bad weather

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Loading an umpire with miserable weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a load, but it is the old sense of a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden, in music, is a chorus repeated after each verse, a synonym.

clue.text: Jack, stableworker, runs away to jog

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: says the piece is taken out

parts.note: an ostler looks after horses at an inn
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A stable hand called Jack fleeing for a quick jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' drops R (runs, in cricket scoring) from OSTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: To jostle is to push or bump against, and jog can mean nudge or bump.

clue.text: Book substitute before a Liverpool fan's turned up?

parts.note: ERE is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwards means read backwards

parts.note: Liverpool FC are the Reds, so a supporter is a Red; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Liverpool supporter turning up with a gadget instead of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-reader is a device for reading digital books, taking the place of printed ones.

clue.text: Sneak out of place after 60% of force deserted

indicators.note: the rearranged piece follows the other
takes three letters of a five-letter word, from the start
letters out of place are jumbled, so sneak is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneak shifting out once most of the troops had left.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' keeps FOR from FORCE; 'out of place' rearranges SNEAK as SAKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means abandoned, left alone, a synonym of deserted.

clue.text: Unplanned commercial wine broadcast

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: says the word is spoken out, giving its sound

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A wine advert going out on air without planning.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK spoken sounds like the Latin HOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'for this', the phrase describes something arranged for the occasion, improvised.

clue.text: One espousing leather trousers?

indicators.note: as a verb, trousers means pockets, so the words hold the answer

explanation.surface: Someone marrying a pair of leather trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb: the phrase pockets the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one, as opposed to several.

clue.text: Smile and start to detest the nine-to-five?

parts.note: a grin is a smile

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Grin and bear it while loathing the office job.
explanation.definitionFit: The grind is tedious routine work, typified by the office day running nine to five.

clue.text: American exposed hero as addict

parts.note: US is United States, American

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, a word is exposed

explanation.surface: An American revealed a hero to be an addict.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who takes drugs, an addict in slang.

clue.text: Ace party? Shame!

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay at a disappointing party.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them embarrassed, to shame them as a verb.

clue.text: Sit and fete DI upset, as given in evidence

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked into a new order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective inspector unsettled at a party, as recorded in evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something testified has been stated under oath, given as evidence.

clue.text: Revolutionary, 20, adopting line 'I'm in charge of support!'

parts.note: Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary

indicators.note: taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the answer to clue 20

explanation.surface: A rebel with a gadget declaring himself head of the support crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts L inside the answer to 20 after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerleader leads a crowd's cheering, in charge of the support for a team.
